description: One source of truth for what any build installs. Every `pip install -r` in a Dockerfile, a workflow or the Makefile must name a requirements file declared here; a target with lock_status 'present' must install its lockfile with --require-hashes; a target with lock_status 'pending' must record the command that closes it, and the pending set may only shrink. tools/check_dependency_contract.py is the gate.

code-sandbox-image.purpose: the network-isolated image untrusted code runs in

container-runtime.pending_reason: requirements/core.txt names seven distributions requirements_lock.txt has never resolved (aiofiles, orjson, ollama, backoff, colorlog, celery, redis), so the lock cannot be derived from it. Until a linux resolution exists the image installs core.txt constrained by requirements/lock/container-constraints.txt, which pins every package the two sets share to the version the release lane ships. The constraint file is derived from the lock rather than being it, because pip refuses a constraint carrying extras or hashes.
container-runtime.closed_by: pip-compile --allow-unsafe --generate-hashes --output-file=requirements/lock/container-runtime.txt requirements/core.txt (run on linux/amd64 with cpython 3.12)

ci-gates.purpose: the offline gate runners; no model or GUI stack
ci-gates.unlocked_reason: the gate jobs resolve fresh on purpose, so a dependency that stops resolving is caught by CI rather than pinned out of sight

developer.purpose: make setup / make setup-dev on a workstation
developer.unlocked_reason: a workstation tracks upstream; the release lane is what must be reproducible
